paragraphs.title: The City of Salvation and the Humbling of the Exalted City

answers: As a strong city with salvation
easy.explanation: The verse says, “We have a strong city; salvation will God appoint for walls and bulwarks.”
easy.q: How is the city of Judah described in the song?

answers: The inhabitants of the lofty city
easy.explanation: The verse commands the gates to be opened so that “the righteous nation” may enter.
easy.q: Who is to enter through the gates?

easy.explanation: The passage says that the feet of the poor and needy shall tread the city down.
easy.q: Who will tread down the lofty city?

answers: Because it is a powerful army
medium.explanation: The nation is described as one “which keepeth the truth.”
medium.q: Why may the righteous nation enter through the gates?

medium.explanation: “Lofty” means high or exalted; the city is then brought down to the ground.
medium.q: What does “lofty” mean in “the lofty city”?

answers: One is protected by salvation, while the other is humbled
One is in the wilderness, while the other is by the sea
One is wealthy, while the other is poor
medium.explanation: The city of Judah has salvation for its walls, while the lofty city is brought low.
medium.q: What is the main contrast between the two cities?

answers: It is reserved only for kings
challenge.explanation: The gates are opened so that the righteous nation may enter.
challenge.q: What do the open gates reveal about the character of the city of salvation?

answers: Power and pride do not last forever
challenge.explanation: The city's humiliation shows the downfall of human pride and power.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the city being brought down to the dust?

answers: The weak walk over the once-proud city
challenge.explanation: The feet of the poor and needy tread down the city that had been lofty.
challenge.q: How does the mention of the poor and needy strengthen the theme of the city's humiliation?

paragraphs.title: The Righteous Path and God’s Judgment

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The way of the just is uprightness.”
easy.q: How is the way of the just described?

easy.explanation: The people desire God’s name and the remembrance of Him.
easy.q: What does the people’s soul desire?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Lord, thou wilt ordain peace for us.”
easy.q: What does the Lord ordain for His people?

answers: To direct or make the path right
medium.explanation: The expression presents God as measuring, directing, or making the path of the just right.
medium.q: What does “weigh the path” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: When God’s judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
medium.q: Why do the people wait for God’s judgments?

medium.explanation: Even when favor is shown to him, the wicked still refuses to learn righteousness.
medium.q: Why does the wicked not receive lasting favor in the passage?

answers: God’s judgments cause the inhabitants of the world to learn righteousness
God’s judgments remove the need for righteousness
challenge.explanation: The verse directly says that the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness when God’s judgments are in the earth.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between God’s judgments and learning righteousness?

answers: The just walk uprightly, while the wicked refuse to learn righteousness
They both follow the same path
challenge.explanation: The just have an upright way, while the wicked continues to deal unjustly and will not learn righteousness.
challenge.q: What contrast is shown between the just and the wicked?

answers: They credit God with their peace and all their works
They say peace happened by itself
They seek to turn away from God
challenge.explanation: The people acknowledge that God has ordained peace and wrought all their works in them.
challenge.q: How do the people’s words about peace show their recognition of God’s work?

paragraphs.title: Remembering God in Distress and Hoping for Resurrection

easy.explanation: The people say, “other lords beside thee have had dominion over us.”
easy.q: Whom does the people say once had dominion over them?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Lord, in trouble have they visited thee.”
easy.q: To whom does the people turn in trouble?

answers: The dead shall live and arise
easy.explanation: The verse declares, “Thy dead men shall live” and “they shall arise.”

medium.explanation: The words refer to the deceased, who are contrasted with the hope that they will live and arise.
medium.q: In this passage, what are “the dead” and those who dwell in dust?

medium.explanation: The people compare their distress to the pain and cries of a woman in labor.
medium.q: What does the image of a woman in childbirth describe?

answers: They did not bring deliverance or cause the inhabitants to fall
medium.explanation: The people say, “we have not wrought any deliverance in the earth.”
medium.q: What was the result of the people’s efforts according to verse 18?

answers: From remembering bondage and distress to hoping for resurrection
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from former masters and trouble to the hope that the dead will live and arise.
challenge.q: What is the main movement from verse 13 to verse 19?

challenge.explanation: The people declare that they will make mention of God’s name alone.
challenge.q: What does the statement “by thee only will we make mention of thy name” express?

answers: It suggests freshness and life coming to those who dwell in the dust
It represents the destruction of the land
It prevents the dead from rising
challenge.explanation: The dew of herbs is a life-giving image accompanying the earth’s casting out of the dead.
challenge.q: How does the dew image relate to resurrection?

paragraphs.title: Hiding During the Wrath and the Earth’s Revelation

easy.explanation: The people are told to enter their chambers, shut the doors, and hide.
easy.q: What are the people commanded to do before the indignation passes?

easy.explanation: The command says, “hide thyself as it were for a little moment.”
easy.q: How long is the hiding described as lasting?

easy.explanation: The earth will disclose its blood and will no longer cover its slain.

answers: To judge and bring consequences for sin
medium.explanation: The Lord comes out of His place to judge the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity.
medium.q: What does “to punish” mean in the statement about the inhabitants of the earth?

answers: To wait until the indignation has passed
medium.explanation: They are told to hide for a little moment until the indignation is overpast.
medium.q: Why are the people told to hide?

answers: The people hide, the Lord comes to punish, and the earth reveals the blood
The earth reveals the blood, the people hide, and the Lord comes
The Lord builds a city, the people hide, and the earth is restored
medium.explanation: First the people are told to hide; then the Lord comes to punish; finally the earth discloses its blood.
medium.q: What is the order of events in the passage?

answers: The people are temporarily protected while judgment is revealed
The people must hide their own crimes
The earth protects the slain forever
challenge.explanation: The people hide while God brings judgment and the earth exposes what it had concealed.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the closed doors and the earth’s revelation of blood?

answers: The hidden blood and slain will be exposed
The earth will cover everything again
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the earth will no longer conceal the blood and the slain.
challenge.q: What does “shall no more cover her slain” emphasize?

answers: The indignation is a time when the Lord judges the sins of the inhabitants
It is only a time of trade and peace
It is when the people abandon their faith
challenge.explanation: The passage connects the Lord’s coming indignation with punishing the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the coming indignation and the punishment of the earth’s inhabitants?
